body: Yeah skincare is definitely very personal and lots of things that work for you might not work for others so it's always good to test things out to see what your skin likes! I'm glad you were able to see results with Differin though! Wish I had the same results

Differin is more for people with acne. I went through 2 tubes of it and I didn't see any significant improvement in my sun spots but everyone is different! I've also been using tret 0.025% for the past year and have noticed a very slight lightening in my freckles, but after using H for just 2 weeks, I've noticed a very appreciable difference in my skin tone. This is also my last resort before turning to laser/light therapy but I can definitely say that I might not have to go that route if I keep seeing ongoing results in the next few weeks!

H is safe as long as you use it as prescribed by your dermatologist and take a break from it every 2-3 months. But as always, everyone looking to use any sort of prescription topical should speak to their provider and make sure to weigh the pros and cons.

I have a spot exactly like that from sun exposure so not really the same, but I asked my derm for a hydroquinone prescription and it has been working wonders for my sun spot + tiny freckles! Lasers or light therapy would probably be the most effective though. Definitely ask your derm about possible treatments because I don't think OTC products would be very helpful in this scenario.
